questions.question: Basic use cases Xu lists for a URL shortener include:
options: Only deleting URLs with no create or redirect paths in real production systems at scale.
Shorten long→short, redirect short→long, plus HA/scalability/fault tolerance.
Training ML models on video frames exclusively in real production systems at scale.
Replacing DNS for the entire public internet in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: URL shortening… URL redirecting… High availability, scalability, and fault tolerance

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: URL shortening… URL redirecting… High availability, scalability, and fault tolerance

questions.question: A 301 redirect implies the short URL mapping is treated as:
options: Temporary, so every later click still hits the shortener first.
Permanent, so browsers may cache and skip the shortener later.
Invalid, so clients must poll with HTTP 100 Continue in real production systems at scale.
Encrypted, so only POST can resolve the alias in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: A 301 redirect shows that the requested URL is “permanently” moved

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: A 301 redirect shows that the requested URL is “permanently” moved

questions.question: A reason to prefer 302 over 301 for a shortener is:
options: 302 always reduces shortener load more than 301 in real production systems at scale.
302 keeps traffic flowing through the shortener for easier click analytics.
302 disables HTTPS for all subsequent navigations in real production systems at scale.
302 stores the long URL only in the DNS CNAME record in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: if analytics is important, 302 redirect is a better choice

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: if analytics is important, 302 redirect is a better choice

questions.question: Xu’s example shortened URL charset is described as:
options: Only emoji and whitespace characters in real production systems at scale.
Digits 0-9 and letters a-z / A-Z (base62-style).
Only hexadecimal with mandatory dashes every two chars.
Only Morse code transmitted over SMS in real production systems at scale.
questions.explanation: combination of numbers (0-9) and characters (a-z, A-Z)

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide
reference.excerpt: combination of numbers (0-9) and characters (a-z, A-Z)

questions.question: With 100M new URLs/day, write QPS is roughly:
options: 100 million writes per second sustained all day in real production systems at scale.
About 100M/86400 ≈ ~1k+ writes/sec order of magnitude (Xu ~1160).
Exactly 2 writes per second regardless of assumptions in real production systems at scale.
Zero writes because shorteners only redirect in real production systems at scale.
